comparison: Both strongly support the central finding of precise matching in axon-coupled spine pairs (C3-C5, C35-C42). OpenEval emphasizes regression slopes near 1 and statistical significance (KS p=0.018, p=0.0002). Peer reviewers explicitly affirmed this as 'a very important confirmation' with 'convincing' results reproduced across three animals. Peer review also includes neck diameter findings (C70-C71) which OpenEval addresses separately in R12.

Perfect agreement on specificity of matching effect (C47-C51). Both support that different-dendrite pairs and random pairs show no correlation, providing important negative controls. OpenEval notes n=127 for different-dendrite pairs. Peer reviewer found this unsurprising and expected, accepting the finding without challenge.

Perfect agreement on glial proximity analysis (C52-C56). Both support that glial proximity does not explain spine size matching precision. OpenEval notes non-significant KS test p-values across four categories. Peer reviewers accepted without challenge, though noted some figures were redundant.

Both address methods (C95-C111), but with different evaluations. OpenEval finds methods comprehensive and rigorous with appropriate statistical approaches. Peer reviewers raised concerns about ordering spines by size before correlation analysis (inducing artificial correlation) and requested clarification on 'dendritic branch' vs 'dendrite' terminology, marking this as UNCERTAIN.

Both address information-theoretic calculation (C6-C7, C57-C59, C114), but with different assessments. OpenEval finds the mathematical framework sound and calculation transparent. Peer reviewer requested more detailed explanation in Results section and discussion of varying discrimination thresholds, indicating the analysis was insufficiently explained rather than fundamentally flawed (UNCERTAIN vs SUPPORTED).

Both address time-averaging model (C8, C60-C64), but with different levels of confidence. OpenEval supports the binomial statistics calculations as mathematically correct while noting they represent lower bounds. Peer reviewer expressed confusion about the logic, particularly regarding release probability during bursts, marking this UNCERTAIN vs OpenEval's SUPPORTED.

Both address contextualization of findings (C65-C68, C74). OpenEval supports methodological improvements and statistical interpretation. Peer reviewers explicitly praised methodology, noting reproduction across three animals and high p-values as convincing. Both agree on the strength of the statistical evidence and replication.

Both address spine morphological correlations (C16-C21). OpenEval supports comprehensive correlation analysis with appropriate statistical methods. Peer reviewers accepted these basic characterization results without challenge, noting 'data were carefully and creatively analyzed.' Peer R5 also includes presynaptic correlations (C24-C27) which OpenEval addresses in R2.

Both address distributional properties of spine features (C29-C34, C44). OpenEval supports the characterization of skewed distributions and justification for log-normal transformations. Peer reviewers accepted these descriptive findings without challenge, with overall positive assessment of the analysis.

Both address comparative context claims (C73-C76). OpenEval supports comparisons with neocortex and mouse cortex data, noting order of magnitude improvement over release probability estimates. Peer reviewers accepted these contextualizing observations without challenge, consistent with overall positive assessment.

Both address CaMKII mechanism (C81-C86). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN, noting the convergence of time scales is suggestive but speculative, requiring additional validation. Peer reviewers supported the underlying biochemical mechanisms without challenge, though they questioned the time-averaging calculations separately (in R4).

Both address speculative interpretations about information encoding and computational analogies (C77-C78, C89-C94). OpenEval marks as UNCERTAIN, noting these are discussion points lacking direct experimental support. Peer reviewers accepted these theoretical frameworks without specific critique (SUPPORTED), suggesting different thresholds for evaluating speculative content.

Partial overlap on dendritic compartmentalization speculation (C77-C78). OpenEval groups this with other speculative claims and marks UNCERTAIN. Peer reviewer implicitly supported this interpretation by noting it would be 'surprising' if same-axon synapses on different dendrites were not better correlated, acknowledging dendritic compartmentalization importance.

OpenEval R5 addresses scale-invariant precision (C43-C44, C46) with constant CV of 0.083, marking as SUPPORTED. Peer R1 includes these claims as part of the broader central finding evaluation, also marking SUPPORTED. Both agree on the importance of constant precision across size range.

OpenEval R12 addresses unexpected neck diameter control findings (C69-C72), marking as SUPPORTED with reasonable interpretation. Peer R1 includes neck diameter claims (C70-C71) as part of the central finding evaluation, also SUPPORTED. Both accept the high correlation in axon-coupled pairs despite weak population-level correlation.

OpenEval R2 addresses presynaptic-postsynaptic correlations (C22-C28), marking as SUPPORTED. Peer R5 includes some presynaptic correlations (C24-C27) as part of basic characterization, also SUPPORTED. Both accept these correlation findings without challenge.

OpenEval R14 addresses methodological decision to exclude three-synapse MSB configurations (C79-C80), marking as SUPPORTED with appropriate justification. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims.
